strengths: Clear problem motivation with well-demonstrated complementary strengths of text-based vs. visually-grounded reasoning modes
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8 diverse benchmarks with extensive baseline comparisons and thorough ablations
Strong empirical results: AdaVaR-7B surpasses GPT-4o on average; consistent improvements across all benchmarks for 7B model
Elegant technical design with unified prefix-based mode representation enabling natural mode control
Exemplary reproducibility with complete prompts, detailed hyperparameters, and comprehensive supplementary materials
Deep analysis of learned behavior including fine-grained mode selection, attention visualization, and error categorization
Well-structured writing with effective presentation and clear problem formulation
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: prefix-based control, Gaussian-based advantage calculation, and GRPO adaptation are incremental; contribution primarily in engineering rather than novel algorithms
Scope restricted to two reasoning modes only; claims about 'general visual reasoning' limited; width/depth extensions theoretical rather than empirical
Mode-switching mechanism lacks quantitative analysis; appears to provide AdaVaR advantages unavailable to baselines, raising evaluation fairness concerns
Significant gap to oracle upper bound (MathVista: 69.8 vs 74.8; MathVision: 24.5 vs 30.9) suggests fundamental mode selection limitations
Mode selection mechanism concerns: attention analysis shows 97% weight on text tokens vs. 3% on images, suggesting visual information underutilized and mode selection primarily text-driven
Limited theoretical justification for design choices: why is mode-relative advantage via Gaussian CDF optimal? Curriculum strategy appears ad-hoc
Generalization unvalidated: all experiments on Qwen2.5-VL base model only; no evidence of transfer to other LVLMs
Marginal improvements on some benchmarks and lack of statistical significance testing undermine some performance claims
